newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: IAEA plans new step to curb nuclear weapons.
newsitem.headline: IAEA plans new step to curb nuclear weapons.

text.p: The International Atomic Energy Agency said on Monday it was about to take a major step in improving nuclear non-proliferation safeguards.

Addressing the United Nations nuclear agency's annual forum in Vienna, director general Hans Blix gave no details but said a special committee would meet next month to accelerate work on non-proliferation.
The aim would be to give inspectors greater access to data from the 120 states that had signed comprehensive safety agreements.
Blix added the new measure was "essential to introduce new cost-effective methods and to provide vitally needed confidence that commitments are fully respected."
The agency's immediate priorities were to complete safeguard agreements with North Korea -- currently under discussion -- and to continue its nuclear inspections in Iraq, he said.
Another issue likely to be raised at the forum is the transport of radioactive material by air.

The IAEA last week approved new safety standards for the containers used to ferry radioactive material by air, prompting concern among environmental groups which fear the containers would not be strong enough to withstand a crash.
"The new IAEA standard is a sham," said Paul Leventhal, president of the Washington-based Nuclear Control Institute in a statement faxed to Reuters in Vienna.

"This action demonstrates a greater concern with the economic toll to the plutonium industry of developing a truly crash-worthy cask than the human toll if a plutonium transport plane crashes into a densely populated area."
The ex-Soviet Republic Moldova, which has no nuclear capacity, applied for IAEA membership at the opening session, attended by delegates from over 100 countries.
Moldovan President Mircea Snegur is to address the forum during a three-day official visit to Austria starting on Wednesday.
